nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the canopy and the gaps in it drives growth of the forest trees and herbs that everything else feeds on.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: The park is very wet, with roughly 2,000 to over 4,000 mm of rain a year, which sustains the lowland rainforest.

nodes.name: Forest soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients recycled from leaf litter and dead animals are taken up quickly by forest roots.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the forest soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit through much of the year and are eaten by primates, turacos, hornbills and elephants, so many animals depend on them.

nodes.name: Myrianthus trees
nodes.desc: A recorded understory tree of the Cross River forests with edible fruit; fleshy forest fruits like this feed primates and rodents.

nodes.name: Sorindeia trees
nodes.desc: A forest tree whose fruit has been recorded as food for the Guinea turaco, piping hornbill and African green pigeon.

nodes.name: Aframomum herbs
nodes.desc: Ground-layer herbs of the ginger family. On Afi Mountain they made up most of the diet of Cross River gorillas.

nodes.name: Cross River gorilla
nodes.desc: A rare gorilla of the Nigeria-Cameroon border hills. It eats fruit, herbs, bark and leaves, switching to herbs when fruit is scarce.

nodes.name: Drill
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey that prefers fruit, including figs, and also eats leaves, seeds, mushrooms and invertebrates such as ants.

nodes.name: Chimpanzee
nodes.desc: An ape of the forest canopy and floor that eats mostly fruit, and also leaves and some animal prey.

nodes.name: Preuss's red colobus
nodes.desc: A rare leaf-eating monkey of the Cameroon-Nigeria forests, living high in the canopy.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats leaves, bark and fruit, and spreads the seeds of many trees in its dung, shaping forest tree diversity.

nodes.name: Great blue turaco
nodes.desc: A large forest bird that eats fruit, flowers and leaves, including figs, and spreads seeds in its droppings.

nodes.name: Piping hornbill
nodes.desc: A noisy canopy hornbill, among the best-recorded birds around the park, that mainly eats forest fruit.

nodes.name: Forest giant squirrel
nodes.desc: Forages for fruits and seeds of trees and lianas, cracking tough nuts, plus a few insects.

nodes.name: Tullberg's soft-furred mouse
nodes.desc: A small forest rodent that forages on the forest floor and is prey for genets and snakes.

nodes.name: Crested servaline genet
nodes.desc: A small forest carnivore. A GloBI record shows it eating Tullberg's soft-furred mouse.

nodes.name: Ball python
nodes.desc: A constrictor that eats rodents and other small vertebrates; recorded prey includes forest rodents and the forest giant squirrel.

nodes.name: Nile monitor
nodes.desc: A generalist reptile that eats fish, frogs, birds, eggs, rodents and invertebrates, and will also scavenge carrion.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: In African rainforests leopards mostly take duikers and primates, and also rodents and other mammals.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A forest eagle whose main prey is monkeys, including colobus species, along with duikers.
